evidence.claim: The calibration of the chaotic-torque distribution is based on gravitational-instability simulations of protoplanetary disks, not MRI-driven AGN disks, and the scaling parameters C and N_max are adopted heuristically without first-principles or simulation-based mapping to the physical system being modeled.
evidence.excerpt: The entire torque-distribution machinery is calibrated against Wu et al. (2024)'s gravitational-instability simulations of protoplanetary disks (PPDs), but the physical setup in the paper is MRI-driven turbulence in AGN disks (Sec. 2, Sec. 3, Sec. 5.1). The free parameter C "captures the strength of MRI with respect to GI" (Sec. 4) but no first-principles or simulation-based mapping between GI's σ_T_turb and MRI's σ_T_turb is provided — C is varied in {10^2, 10^{2.5}, 10^3} as a heuristic. The persistence-length parameter N_max is also fixed at 100 from a GI simulation (Sec. 4 — "chosen based upon how often the torque changes magnitude or sign in Wu et al. 2024"), and σ_turb ∝ √N_max in Eq. (16), so this calibration is load-bearing for every reported bound.
